about.title: Stockton Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Stockton is a working city, and the things people rely on here get used hard: tools on job sites, appliances at home, car seats buckled in for the drive down Hammer Lane or March Lane. When one of those items fails because it was badly designed, built wrong, or sold without a proper warning, California law treats the situation differently than an ordinary accident. Under strict liability, you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. What matters is whether the product was defective and whether that defect hurt you. Responsibility can reach the company that made it, the distributor that shipped it, and the store in San Joaquin County that put it on the shelf. Some of Stockton's 1,313 injury collisions in 2025 may have involved a component that failed rather than a driver, and those cases turn on physical evidence. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that pairs injured Stockton residents with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency, with no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Stockton Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: You generally do not have to show the maker was negligent, only that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that it caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with build cases around that standard.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Can Answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Stockton or San Joaquin County retailer that sold the product may all share responsibility under California law. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: The Product Is the Proof
items.desc: Keeping the failed item, its packaging, and any receipts is often the single most important step. The attorneys in our network know how to preserve and examine that evidence before it disappears.

items.question: My airbag never deployed in a crash on El Dorado Street. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. The collision itself may involve another driver, while the airbag failure may point to a defect in the vehicle or a component. Stockton recorded 1,938 people injured in collisions during 2025, and in some of those cases a part that did not work as designed made the injuries worse. Do not have the car repaired or scrapped until an attorney has had a chance to inspect it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was faulty?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability commonly runs on strict liability, which means the focus is on whether the product was defective and whether that defect injured you. Showing what the company knew or how carefully it acted is generally not required, though it can still matter in some situations.

items.question: I already threw the broken product away. Can I still do anything?
items.answer: Possibly, but it makes the claim harder, so stop and gather whatever remains: packaging, manuals, receipts, photos, order confirmations, and the names of anyone who saw the failure. If the item is in a dumpster or with a repair shop in Stockton, try to retrieve it before it is gone. An attorney can advise you on what is still workable based on what you have.
